ui.agents.models.reading.title.role: Section heading in a team's detail pane
ui.agents.models.reading.title.tone: Plain noun phrase naming two technical readings
ui.agents.models.reading.title.note: Names the block that answers which model and reasoning effort each team member will run on, and which layer chose them.

ui.agents.models.reading.description.role: One-line explanation under the same heading
ui.agents.models.reading.description.tone: Neutral statement of what the columns below show
ui.agents.models.reading.description.note: The table gives a member, the model it resolves to, and the reasoning effort, each with the layer that set it.

ui.agents.models.reading.member_col.note: Same word the roster table above uses for the same column, so the two tables read as one picture.

ui.agents.models.reading.model_col.note: The model identifier this member will launch on, or the phrase for inheriting the session's.

ui.agents.models.reading.effort_col.note: A reasoning effort is one of the ladder words the backend accepts; it is not the model tier, which appears inside the model cell.

ui.agents.models.reading.session_model.role: Reading for a member that inherits the launching session's model
ui.agents.models.reading.session_model.tone: Lowercase phrase that stands in for a model identifier
ui.agents.models.reading.session_model.note: The backend answers a null model with its source set to the session for a slot with no tier, and with the tier source for a tier that resolves to the session. This phrase carries the fact in both cases; no layer word is printed beside it when the session really is the only layer.

ui.agents.models.reading.not_resolved.role: Reading for a member whose model could not be resolved at all
ui.agents.models.reading.not_resolved.note: Used on an unavailable member instead of a model identifier, because the row below its reading carries the backend's reason. The alternative - printing the model layer - would claim a resolution that does not exist.

ui.agents.models.reading.tier_layer.role: The tier in play and the layer that set it, under a model value
ui.agents.models.reading.tier_layer.note: A model tier is a routing word (lo, med, hi), not a reasoning effort and not a model name. It is what chose the model beside it, so it reads as that model's provenance.

placeholders.tier: Tier identifier from the backend (lo, med or hi); do not translate the identifier.
placeholders.source: One of the layer phrases below, already translated (from this team, from the agent); interpolate as-is.

ui.agents.models.reading.effort_auto.role: The reasoning effort of a member whose request was auto
ui.agents.models.reading.effort_auto.tone: Lowercase phrase with the operator's own word in parentheses
ui.agents.models.reading.effort_auto.note: auto means the model's own default, NOT the tier map's level, and the two differ for most models. Printing the resolved level alone would read as though the operator had set that level by hand, which is exactly the confusion this phrase prevents. The literal word auto is the wire's word and stays untranslated.

ui.agents.models.reading.effort_clamped.role: The requested effort as clamped by the model's ladder
ui.agents.models.reading.effort_clamped.note: Shown only when the model clamps the request to a different level. Both words are ladder identifiers from the backend and stay untranslated; the arrow means was asked for, runs at.

placeholders.requested: The effort identifier the operator set; do not translate.
placeholders.value: The effort identifier the child will actually run at; do not translate.

ui.agents.models.reading.effort_default.role: The reasoning effort when nothing was requested
ui.agents.models.reading.effort_default.note: The weakest layer: no effort was asked for anywhere, so the chosen model's built-in default applies. Used as the effort cell's value when the backend could not name a level.

ui.agents.models.reading.unavailable.role: Warning that a member could not start as configured
ui.agents.models.reading.unavailable.tone: Warning, stating the consequence then the backend's own reason
ui.agents.models.reading.unavailable.note: Sits inside the member's own row in the reading table, so it cannot be attributed to the member below it. The reason text is the backend's own sentence and is not translated.

placeholders.reason: Backend sentence naming what is wrong with the tier; interpolate unchanged.

ui.agents.models.reading.unavailable_edi.role: The same warning inside the edit form, where the controls are the draft
ui.agents.models.reading.unavailable_edi.tone: Warning that names the reading it describes as the SAVED one
ui.agents.models.reading.unavailable_edi.note: The form's selects may hold unsaved changes, so this warning must not read as a statement about what is on screen. It describes the saved definition, and says so.

placeholders.reason: Backend sentence naming what is wrong with the tier; interpolate unchanged.

ui.agents.models.reading.unavailable_hin.role: The remedy beside an unavailable member's reason
ui.agents.models.reading.unavailable_hin.tone: Short instruction naming the settings surface only
ui.agents.models.reading.unavailable_hin.note: The backend's reason names the config key (subagents.models); this names where a person changes it, which is what the operator needs. Same remedy the agent refusals use for an unconfigured tier.

ui.agents.models.reading.read_failed.role: Notice that the effective reading could not be fetched
ui.agents.models.reading.read_failed.tone: Neutral statement of a failed read
ui.agents.models.reading.read_failed.note: Used when the probe failed for a reason other than the route's absence, which is also why the override controls are hidden. A backend that predates the route says nothing instead.

ui.agents.models.reading.saved_label.role: Label on the saved-reading caption in the edit form
ui.agents.models.reading.saved_label.note: Marks the line under a member's controls as the STORED resolution rather than the draft's, so Inherit and a changed select both have a visible meaning.

ui.agents.models.reading.model_cell.role: The saved model in the edit form's caption
ui.agents.models.reading.model_cell.tone: Label and value on one line
ui.agents.models.reading.model_cell.note: One message with a placeholder rather than a label glued to a value in code, so a translator can reorder or inflect the pair.

placeholders.value: A model identifier, or the phrase for inheriting the session's model; the identifier is not translated.

ui.agents.models.reading.effort_cell.role: The saved reasoning effort in the edit form's caption
ui.agents.models.reading.effort_cell.tone: Label and value on one line
ui.agents.models.reading.effort_cell.note: The companion of the model cell; the value is a ladder identifier, the auto phrase, or the model default phrase.

placeholders.value: A reasoning-effort identifier or one of the effort phrases above; identifiers are not translated.

ui.agents.models.source.team.role: Layer label: the team set this value
ui.agents.models.source.team.tone: Lowercase phrase read inside a line
ui.agents.models.source.team.note: The team here means this team's own member override, the strongest layer a roster entry owns.

ui.agents.models.source.row.role: Layer label: the agent or team row set this value
ui.agents.models.source.row.tone: Lowercase phrase read inside a line
ui.agents.models.source.row.note: The row is the agent's own registry entry and its effort tag, which applies to the member wherever it is used.

ui.agents.models.source.none.role: Layer label: nothing set the tier
ui.agents.models.source.none.tone: Lowercase phrase read inside a line
ui.agents.models.source.none.note: Means no tier is in play at all, so the model comes from the launching session.

ui.agents.models.source.tier.role: Layer label: the tier map set this value
ui.agents.models.source.tier.tone: Lowercase noun phrase read inside a line
ui.agents.models.source.tier.note: The tier map is the tier-to-model-and-effort table configured in Settings. The phrase names that table rather than translating the word tier.

ui.agents.models.source.session.role: Layer label: the launching session set this value
ui.agents.models.source.session.tone: Lowercase noun phrase read inside a line
ui.agents.models.source.session.note: Printed only where the session is not already named by the value itself, so the pane never says session twice in one cell.

ui.agents.models.source.model_default.role: Layer label: the model's own default set this value
ui.agents.models.source.model_default.tone: Lowercase possessive phrase read inside a line
ui.agents.models.source.model_default.note: The weakest layer: no effort was requested, so the chosen model's built-in default applies. Also the layer behind an auto request, which is why it is the phrase the auto cell pairs with.

ui.agents.models.override.tier_label.role: Accessible name of one member's model-tier select
ui.agents.models.override.tier_label.tone: Label naming the control and the member it belongs to
ui.agents.models.override.tier_label.note: The visible label sits above the control and names the field; this string is the accessible name, and it must identify the member because every row carries one of these controls.

placeholders.member: Member role name as stored in the team; do not translate the identifier.

ui.agents.models.override.tier_field.role: Visible label above one member's model-tier select
ui.agents.models.override.tier_field.tone: Short noun phrase in the app's sentence case
ui.agents.models.override.tier_field.note: Names the field itself, where the accessible name above also names the member. A bare tier word beside a bare effort word is not self-describing, which is why the field is labelled on screen.

ui.agents.models.override.effort_label.role: Accessible name of one member's reasoning-effort select
ui.agents.models.override.effort_label.tone: Label naming the control and the member it belongs to
ui.agents.models.override.effort_label.note: The same shape as the tier select's accessible name, for the second control in the same row.

placeholders.member: Member role name as stored in the team; do not translate the identifier.

ui.agents.models.override.effort_field.role: Visible label above one member's reasoning-effort select
ui.agents.models.override.effort_field.tone: Short noun phrase in the app's sentence case
ui.agents.models.override.effort_field.note: The companion of the model-tier field label. A reasoning effort is a different vocabulary from a model tier and the two must not be read as one control.

ui.agents.models.override.inherit.role: Select option meaning no override on this layer
ui.agents.models.override.inherit.note: Chosen when the operator wants the layer below to decide; it is the option a member with no override shows, and the word the agent tool uses for clearing a pin.

ui.agents.models.override.auto.role: Select option meaning the model's own default effort
ui.agents.models.override.auto.tone: Capitalised option label with its meaning in parentheses
ui.agents.models.override.auto.note: auto is a value, not the absence of one, and it is not a ladder level: the operator's word is kept beside what it means, because Inherit sits in the same list and the two must not be confused. The word auto itself stays untranslated - it is the wire's vocabulary.

ui.agents.models.pin_reach.role: Note beside an agent's own effort tier, listing the teams that use it
ui.agents.models.pin_reach.tone: Neutral statement of reach, naming the tier as its subject
ui.agents.models.pin_reach.note: Answers what an agent-level tier affects, since it is machine-wide and the teams are where it is felt. Shown only when the agent HAS its own tier, so the sentence's subject is never an inherit.
ui.agents.models.pin_reach.plural_guidance: Use the CLDR branches needed by the target language. Keep the count as a plain argument where it appears, not as a formatted number.

placeholders.count: Number of teams that use this agent; nonnegative integer. Numeric plural selector.
placeholders.teams: Comma-separated team names, already joined; do not translate the names.
